post.caption: A museum's diamond was just glass. In March 2018, Prague's National Museum reported fakes in its gem collection. Its five carat diamond, held since the 1960s, was plain glass cut like one. A nineteen carat sapphire, bought in the 1970s, was synthetic. A real one would be worth tens of millions of crowns today. About half of the museum's rubies turned out to be synthetic too. The museum did not know how the fakes got in. The deputy director suggested a show of fakes found in museums worldwide. The fake sapphire had cost 200,000 crowns.
